title: The Growth Kinetic and Ultra High Hardness of CoCrFeNiTi High–Entropy Alloy by Mechanical Alloying and Spark Plasma Sintering

recollection.starting_material: Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, Ti elemental powders (guess)
recollection.intervention: Mechanical alloying followed by Spark Plasma Sintering (guess)
recollection.structure: Single-phase FCC or BCC solid solution with ultra-high hardness (guess)
recollection.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening and grain refinement via severe plastic deformation and rapid sintering (guess)
recollection.results: Hardness values exceeding 1000 HV and detailed growth kinetics of the sintered phase (guess)

score.note: The intervention merely restates the title without milling or SPS conditions. The proposed single-phase structure is incorrect; the alloy was 83% FCC and 17% BCC with sub-48 nm grains. The strengthening explanation correctly identifies solid-solution strengthening and milling-induced grain refinement, though it omits dislocation accumulation, Hall–Petch strengthening, and titanium’s phase-stabilizing role. The claimed hardness above 1000 HV is far from the reported 675 HV, and no correct strength values are given.
